title: Convenium.Design Brand DNA
description: One business's Design DNA: who it is, who it serves, how it should look and sound, and what it needs made. Written by the brand-strategist agent to <project>/.olympus/brand-dna.json (with a readable BRAND.md beside it) and read by design-director to resolve direction and derive DESIGN.md tokens. Lives with the client project, never in the Convenium.Design repo.

mode.description: evidence = built from the business's existing site, socials, documents, media and competitors, plus a short interview. interview-only = no public presence to analyse; built from the interview and supplied material alone.

sources.description: Everything the DNA was built from. A URL counts only if it was actually fetched.

location.description: Where it trades; matters for local businesses (hospitality, retail, services).

offer.description: What it sells, in one or two sentences a customer would recognise.

jobs.description: What they are trying to get done when they meet this business.

positioning.description: Why choose this over the alternatives, in the business's own terms.

lookAndFeel.description: How it presents itself visually — the thing to stand apart from.

goals.description: Business outcomes, primary first (e.g. 'more direct bookings', not 'a nicer site').

primaryAction.description: The one thing a visitor or customer should do.

constraints.description: Must-keep brand assets, legal, platform, budget, deadline.

existingAssets.description: Logo/vector, fonts and licences, photography, video, brand guide, Figma — with paths where supplied.

taste.description: The visual taste profile. Same shape as taste-profile.schema.json (profileId, displayName, source, doctrine, explicitPreferences, avoidList, references, confidence, provenance), produced by convenium-design-taste-interview or convenium-design-style-picker.

why.description: The evidence that points to this doctrine — business, audience and taste, not just taste.

departures.description: Where this business should deviate from the doctrine's defaults, and why.

neededProducts.description: What the business needs made, highest value first. The user confirms this list at Gate A. Only `website` and `brand-identity` have a full pipeline today; other kinds are recorded so later tracks can pick them up.

openQuestions.description: What the strategist could not establish. Never filled with guesses.
